Lizar has a plugin that can retrieve credentials from Internet Explorer and Microsoft Edge using `vaultcmd.exe` and another that can collect RDP access credentials using the `CredEnumerateW` function.
QuasarRAT has the ability to set file attributes to "hidden" to hide files from the compromised user's view in Windows File Explorer.
Lucifer has established persistence by creating the following [REDACTED] `schtasks /create /sc minute /mo 1 /tn QQMusic ^ /tr C:Users\%USERPROFILE%\Downloads\spread.exe /F`.
SYNful Knock can be sent instructions via special packets to change its functionality. Code for new functionality can be included in these messages.
Volt Typhoon has selectively cleared Windows Event Logs, system logs, and other technical artifacts to remove evidence of intrusion activity.
NightClub has used a [REDACTED] in DNS tunneling removing any `=` from the result of base64 encoding, and replacing `/` characters with `-s` and `+` characters with `-p`.
Saint Bot has used `check_registry_keys` as part of its environmental checks.
Saint Bot has created a [REDACTED] named "Maintenance" to establish persistence.
Empire contains modules for executing commands over SSH as well as in-memory VNC agent injection.
Cobalt Group has used the command `[REDACTED].exe /s /ns C:\Users\ADMINI~W\AppData\Local\Temp\XKNqbpzl.txt` to bypass AppLocker and launch a malicious script.
Crimson can use a module to perform [REDACTED] on compromised hosts.
SameCoin can attempt to connect to the Israel Home Front Command site, oref.org[.]il, which is only reachable from within Israel to verify the target's location.
PLEAD has the ability to steal saved passwords from Microsoft Outlook.
FALLCHILL can collect operating system (OS) version information, processor information, and system name from the victim.
During C0027, used RustScan to scan for open ports on targeted ESXi appliances.
XLoader can delete malicious executables from compromised machines.
RAPIDPULSE can transfer files to and from compromised hosts.
Rocke's miner, "TermsHost.exe", evaded defenses by injecting itself into Windows processes, including Notepad.exe.
During Operation MidnightEclipse, threat actors exploited CVE-2024-3400 in Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect.
RedCurl mimicked legitimate file names and scheduled tasks, e.g. ` MicrosoftCurrentupdatesCheck` and `MdMMaintenenceTask` to mask malicious files and scheduled tasks.
Lazarus Group has used [REDACTED] to execute commands and malicious code.
reGeorg has the ability to download files to targeted systems.
INC Ransomware has the ability to use wmic.exe to spread to multiple endpoints within a compromised environment.
HAFNIUM has used MSGraph to exfiltrate data from email, OneDrive, and SharePoint.
The Regin malware platform supports many standard protocols, including SMB.
Lazarus Group has sent malicious links to victims via email.
For Operation Dream Job, Lazarus Group conducted extensive reconnaissance research on potential targets.
OilRig has used net.exe in a script with `net accounts /domain` to find the password policy of a domain.
During Operation Dream Job, Lazarus Group digitally signed their own malware to evade detection.
Kazuar obtains a list of running processes through WMI querying and the `ps` command.
CHIMNEYSWEEP can use an embedded RC4 key to decrypt Windows API function strings.
CANONSTAGER has utilized custom API hashing to obfuscate the Windows APIs being used.
FIN10 has moved laterally using the Local Administrator account.
APT37 has used a credential stealer known as ZUMKONG that can harvest usernames and passwords stored in browsers.
OnionDuke has the capability to use a Denial of Service module.
Silence has been observed making videos of victims to observe bank employees day to day activities.
If Shamoon cannot access shares using current privileges, it attempts access using hard coded, domain-specific credentials gathered earlier in the intrusion.
SombRAT has the ability to download and execute additional payloads.
TYPEFRAME can open the Windows Firewall on the victim’s machine to allow incoming connections.
In 2016, APT28 conducted a distributed denial of service (DDoS) attack against the World Anti-Doping Agency.
WellMess can identify the computer name of a compromised host.
DarkGate has used WMI to execute files over the network and to obtain information about the domain.
APT28 has intentionally deleted computer files to cover their tracks, including with use of the program CCleaner.
CookieMiner has looked for files in the user's home directory with "wallet" in their name using `find`.
BADHATCH can obtain logged user information from a compromised machine and can execute the command `whoami.exe`.
ADVSTORESHELL collects, compresses, encrypts, and exfiltrates data to the C2 server every 10 minutes.
Ixeshe collects the computer name of the victim's system during the initial infection.
Patchwork has obtained and used open-source tools such as QuasarRAT.
Cobalt Strike can inject a variety of payloads into processes dynamically chosen by the adversary.
One variant of CloudDuke uses a Microsoft OneDrive account to exchange commands and stolen data with its operators.
BitPaymer has set the run key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` for persistence.
S-Type has provided the ability to execute shell commands on a compromised host.
Crimson can use a HTTP GET request to download its final payload.
FIN7 has encrypted virtual disk volumes on ESXi servers using a version of Darkside ransomware. Additionally, FIN7 has deployed ransomware as the end payload during big game hunting.
Remcos uses the infected hosts as SOCKS5 proxies to allow for tunneling and proxying.

Gamaredon Group has removed security settings for VBA macro execution by changing registry values `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\\\Security\VBAWarnings` and `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Office\\\Security\AccessVBOM`. Gamaredon Group has also modified Registry keys to hide folders and system files and to add the C2 address under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Console\WindowsUpdate`.
CHOPSTICK includes runtime checks to identify an analysis environment and prevent execution on it.
Kevin can use a custom protocol tunneled through DNS or HTTP.
Hydraq uses basic obfuscation in the form of spaghetti code.
RDAT can communicate with the C2 via subdomains that utilize base64 with character substitutions.
PowerDuke has commands to get the current user's name and SID.
APT32 has used [REDACTED]-based tools, [REDACTED] one-liners, and shellcode loaders for execution.
DynoWiper has used the Microsoft Windows native `FindFirstFile()` and `FindNextFile()` to recursively enumerate directories and files on the system.
Lazarus Group malware IndiaIndia saves information gathered about the victim to a file that is saved in the %TEMP% directory, then compressed, encrypted, and uploaded to a C2 server.
Wiarp creates a backdoor through which remote attackers can open a command line interface.
FIN7 has utilized a variety of tools such as Cobalt Strike, PowerSploit, and the remote management [REDACTED], Atera for targeting efforts.
APT5 has modified legitimate binaries and scripts for Pulse Secure VPNs including the legitimate DSUpgrade.pm file to install the ATRIUM webshell for persistence.
RTM has used spearphishing attachments to distribute its malware.
Empire uses PowerSploit's `Invoke-Kerberoast` to request service tickets and return crackable ticket hashes.
LightSpy uses Apple's built-in AVFoundation Framework library to capture and manage audio recordings then transform them to JSON blobs for exfiltration.

Kimsuky has executed Windows commands by using `cmd` and running batch scripts. Kimsuky has also used `cmd.exe` to automatically open downloaded decoy pdf documents with the system’s default PDF viewer. Kimsuky has utilized malicious payloads to create reverse shells within the victim environment. Kimsuky has also used batch scripts to eventually run QuasarRAT.
Exaramel for Windows stores the backdoor's configuration in the Registry in XML format.
RedCurl has used [REDACTED] emails with malicious files to gain initial access.
APT-C-36 has used encoded and obfuscated files, images, and executables.
Sowbug extracted Word documents from a file server on a victim network.
For Operation CuckooBees, the threat actors obtained publicly-available JSP code that was used to deploy a webshell onto a compromised server.
ROADSWEEP can RC4 encrypt content in blocks on targeted systems.
Grandoreiro can store its configuration in the Registry at `HKCU\Software\` under frequently changing names including `%USERNAME%` and `ToolTech-RM`.
VOID MANTICORE has deleted virtual machines directly from the virtualization platform.
Kimsuky has registered [REDACTED] to spoof targeted organizations and trusted third parties including search engines, web platforms, and cryptocurrency exchanges.
The Ninja loader can call Windows APIs for discovery, process injection, and payload decryption.
BADCALL functions as a [REDACTED] server between the victim and C2 server.
Gorgon Group malware can download additional files from C2 servers.
During Salesforce Data Exfiltration, threat actors registered emails shinycorp@tuta[.]com and shinygroup@tuta[.]com to send victims extortion demands.
macOS.OSAMiner has embedded Stripped Payloads within another run-only Stripped Payloads.
FunnyDream has the ability to discover processes, including `Bka.exe` and `BkavUtil.exe`.
Volt Typhoon has used compromised Cisco and NETGEAR end-of-life SOHO routers implanted with KV [REDACTED] malware to support operations.
Bumblebee can create a [REDACTED] script to enable persistence.
LightSpy encrypts the C2 configuration file using AES with a static key, while the module `.dylib` files use a rolling one-byte encoding for obfuscation.
PLAINTEE uses the `ipconfig /all` command to gather the victim’s IP address.
PoshC2 has modules for keystroke logging and capturing credentials from spoofed Outlook authentication messages.
LunarWeb can use shell commands to discover network adapters and configuration.
Action RAT has the ability to collect the MAC address of an infected host.
Higaisa dropped and added `officeupdate.exe` to scheduled tasks.
ServHelper will attempt to enumerate Windows version and system architecture.
SystemBC has used DNS servers to resolve .bit domains to C2 infrastructure.
CreepyDrive can use legitimate OAuth refresh tokens to authenticate with OneDrive.
The `net start` and `net stop` commands can be used in Net to execute or stop Windows services.
Volt Typhoon has conducted pre-compromise reconnaissance for victim host information.
During ShadowRay, threat actors executed commands on interactive and reverse shells.

Gamaredon Group has tested connectivity between a compromised machine and a C2 server using Ping with commands such as `CSIDL_SYSTEM\cmd.exe /c ping -n 1`. Gamaredon Group has searched the ping records to obtain the C2 address and has used ping to search for the C2’s status.
Earth Lusca collected information on user accounts via the `whoami` command.
Stuxnet can propagate via removable media using an autorun.inf file or the CVE-2010-2568 LNK vulnerability.
APT33 has used a variety of publicly available tools like LaZagne, Mimikatz, and ProcDump to dump credentials.
Lumma Stealer has leveraged legitimate applications to then side-load malicious DLLs during execution.
Chrommme can store captured system information locally prior to exfiltration.
Aria-body has the ability to identify the hostname, computer name, Windows version, processor speed, and machine GUID on a compromised host.
Carberp has exploited multiple Windows vulnerabilities (CVE-2010-2743, CVE-2010-3338, CVE-2010-4398, CVE-2008-1084) and a .NET Runtime Optimization vulnerability for privilege escalation.
Gomir probes arbitrary network endpoints for TCP connectivity.
LuminousMoth has obtained an ARP spoofing [REDACTED] from GitHub.
Operators deploying Netwalker have used batch scripts to retrieve the Netwalker payload.
BadPatch attempts to detect if it is being run in a Virtual Machine (VM) using a WMI query for disk drive name, BIOS, and motherboard information.
MagicRAT stores base64 encoded command and contorl URLs in a configuraiton file, with each URL prefixed with the value `LR02DPt22R`.
SampleCheck5000 can decode and decrypt command line strings and files received through C2.
Ke3chang has gained access through VPNs including with compromised accounts and stolen VPN certificates.
FIN13 has obtained memory dumps with ProcDump to parse and extract credentials from a victim's LSASS process memory with Mimikatz.
FIN7 has compiled a list of victims by filtering companies by revenue using Zoominfo, which is a service that provides business information.
RustyWater has established persistence by adding `C:\ProgramData\CertificationKit.ini` to a Windows startup Registry key or to a Run or RunOnce Registry key.
Ryuk has called `kill.bat` for stopping services, disabling services and killing processes.
OSInfo queries the registry to look for information about Terminal Services.
SILENTTRINITY can [REDACTED] keys, including to enable or disable Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).
Metador has used the Windows command line to execute commands.
FunnyDream has used a service named `WSearch` for execution.
S-Type has attempted to determine if a compromised system was using a Japanese keyboard via the `GetKeyboardType` API call.
Qilin can embed a copy of PsExec within its payload and place it in the %Temp% directory under a randomly generated filename.
LODEINFO can looks for the “en_US” locale on the victim’s machine.
Pandora has the ability to gain system privileges through Windows services.
GravityRAT creates a [REDACTED] to ensure it is re-executed everyday.
TA2541 has used malicious links to cloud and web services to gain execution on victim machines.
FatDuke has used `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\CurrentVersion\Run` to establish persistence.
During C0027, Scattered Spider used compromised Azure credentials for credential theft activity and lateral movement to on-premises systems.
HiddenWasp uses an RC4-like algorithm with an already computed PRGA generated key-stream for network communication.
RegDuke can persist using a WMI consumer that is launched every time a process named WINWORD.EXE is started.
DEATHRANSOM can use loop operations to enumerate directories on a compromised host.
Storm-0501 has used compromised Entra Connect Sync Server to move laterally within the victim environment.
QakBot has hidden code within Excel spreadsheets by turning the font color to white and splitting it across multiple cells.
TRANSLATEXT has used a [REDACTED] to retrieve configurations and commands from a public blog site.
During SharePoint ToolShell Exploitation, threat actors used Mimikatz to dump [REDACTED].
Saint Bot has used different API calls, including `GetProcAddress`, `VirtualAllocEx`, `WriteProcessMemory`, `CreateProcessA`, and `SetThreadContext`.
Gamaredon Group has used an obfuscated PowerShell script that used `System.Reflection.Assembly` to gather and send victim information to the C2.
Manjusaka can execute arbitrary commands passed to it from the C2 controller via `cmd.exe /c`.
DEADWOOD will attempt to masquerade its service execution using benign-looking names such as `ScDeviceEnums`.
During Operation AkaiRyū, MirrorFace used `cmd.exe` to run PowerShell commands to drop additional files on the compromised host.
TONESHELL has used `GetForegroundWindow` to detect virtualization or sandboxes by calling the API twice and comparing each window handle.
DnsSystem can download files to compromised systems after receiving a command with the string `downloaddd`.
ThiefQuest uses the function `kill_unwanted` to obtain a list of running processes and kills each process matching a list of security related processes.
SpicyOmelette has collected data and other information from a compromised host.
ServHelper has commands for adding a remote desktop user and sending RDP traffic to the attacker through a reverse SSH tunnel.
LiteDuke can create persistence by adding a shortcut in the `CurrentVersion\Run` Registry key.
MuddyViper has used HTTP GET requests over port 443 and with the WINHTTP_FLAG_SECURE set to SSL/TLS via the WinHTTP API.
metaMain has used XOR-based encryption for collected files before exfiltration.

If running with elevated privileges, OSX/Shlayer has used the `spctl` command to disable Gatekeeper protection for a downloaded file. OSX/Shlayer can also leverage system links pointing to bash scripts in the downloaded DMG file to bypass Gatekeeper, a flaw patched in macOS 11.3 and later versions. OSX/Shlayer has been Notarized by Apple, resulting in successful passing of additional Gatekeeper checks.
Kapeka writes persistent configuration information to the victim host registry.
Mustang Panda has used China Chopper web shells to maintain access to victims’ environments.
SQLRat relies on users clicking on an embedded image to execute the scripts.
Agent Tesla has routines for exfiltration over SMTP, FTP, and HTTP.
InnaputRAT enumerates directories and obtains file attributes on a system.
AppleJeus has used shell scripts to execute commands after installation and set persistence mechanisms.
Saint Bot has relied on users to execute a malicious attachment delivered via spearphishing.

SPAWNCHIMERA has searched the contents of two [REDACTED] files scanner.py and scanner_legacy.py by searching for specific lines and replacing them with values that reduce their ability to track mismatches or new files.
OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D sets the main loader file’s attributes to hidden.
LAPSUS$ has called victims' help desk to convince the support personnel to reset a privileged account’s credentials.

Medusa Ransomware has the ability to delete itself after execution. Medusa Ransomware also has the ability to delete itself after execution through the command `cmd /c ping localhost -n 3 > nul & del`.
Saint Bear has impersonated government and related entities in both phishing activity and developing web sites with malicious links that mimic legitimate resources.
JumbledPath can communicate over a unique series of connections to send and retrieve data from exploited devices.
Lotus Blossom has used commands such as `netstat` to identify system network connections.
LODEINFO components have been compressed with zip for delivery.
Get2 has the ability to identify running processes on an infected host.
Contagious Interview has leveraged [REDACTED] in the execution of their downloader malware targeting Windows devices using a NodeJS script titled nvidia.js.
SideCopy has executed malware by calling the API function `CreateProcessW`.
Sea Turtle has used tools such as Adminer during intrusions.
During Operation Digital Eye, threat actors used the local.exe tool to view [REDACTED] information.
Uroburos can store configuration information in the Registry including the initialization vector and AES key needed to find and decrypt other Uroburos components.
InvisibleFerret has gathered installed programs and running processes.
LunarWeb can decrypt strings related to communication configuration using RC4 with a static key.
Sandworm Team conducted technical reconnaissance of the Parliament of Georgia's official internet domain prior to its 2019 attack.
SharpDisco has dropped a recent-files stealer plugin to `C:\Users\Public\WinSrcNT\It11.exe`.
NotPetya determines if specific antivirus programs are running on an infected host machine.
APT41 sent spearphishing emails with attachments such as compiled HTML (.chm) files to initially compromise their victims.
HiddenFace can upload files from the victim machine to C2 nodes.
APT29 has used various forms of spearphishing attempting to get a user to click on a [REDACTED].
APT18 actors deleted tools and batch files from victim systems.
Metamorfo has embedded a "vmdetect.exe" executable to identify virtual machines at the beginning of execution.
The "SCOUT" variant of NETEAGLE achieves persistence by adding itself to the `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` Registry key.
Leviathan used [REDACTED] techniques during Leviathan Australian Intrusions.

NETEAGLE will attempt to detect if the infected host is configured to a proxy. If so, NETEAGLE will send beacons via an HTTP POST request. NETEAGLE will also use HTTP to download resources that contain an IP address and Port Number pair to connect to for further C2.
Rover takes screenshots of the compromised system's desktop and saves them to `C:\system\screenshot.bmp` for exfiltration every 60 minutes.
AsyncRAT has been delivered via malicious email attachments.
Caterpillar WebShell can run commands on the compromised asset with CMD functions.

Mustang Panda used Run registry keys with names such as `OneNote Update` to execute legitimate executables that would load through search-order hijacking malicious DLLS to ensure persistence during RedDelta Modified PlugX Infection Chain Operations.

items.t: BOLDMOVE can list information of all files in the system recursively from the root directory or from a specified directory.
YAHOYAH checks for antimalware solution processes on the system.
Dtrack can collect network and active connection information.
Shark can update its configuration to use a different C2 server.
APT38 has used several code packing methods such as Themida, Enigma, VMProtect, and Obsidium, to pack their implants.
FIN7 has started the SSH service by executing `sc start sshd`.
Shai-Hulud has leveraged compromised accounts to log into cloud services to access cloud hosted repositories.
Saint Bot has written its payload into a newly-created `EhStorAuthn.exe` process using `ZwWriteVirtualMemory` and executed it using `NtQueueApcThread` and `ZwAlertResumeThread`.
Wizard Spider has shut down or uninstalled security applications on victim systems that might prevent ransomware from executing.

Prestige can delete the backup catalog from the target system using: `c:\Windows\System32\wbadmin.exe delete catalog -quiet` and can also delete volume shadow copies using: `\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet`.
Aria-body has the ability to delete files and directories on compromised hosts.
BlackByte Ransomware spreads itself laterally by writing the JavaScript launcher file to mapped shared folders.
APT5 has used malware with [REDACTED] capabilities to monitor the communications of targeted entities.
Wizard Spider has used WMI to identify anti-virus products installed on a victim's machine.

Troll Stealer collects all data in victim `.ssh` folders by creating a compressed copy that is subsequently exfiltrated to command and control infrastructure. Troll Stealer also collects key information associated with the Government Public Key Infrastructure (GPKI) service for South Korean government information systems.

During the 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack, Sandworm Team remotely discovered systems over LAN connections. OT systems were visible from the IT network as well, giving adversaries the ability to discover operational assets.
RDAT has created a service when it is installed on the victim machine.
During Operation Dream Job, Lazarus Group used malicious Trojans and DLL files to exfiltrate data from an infected host.
Skidmap has the ability to replace the pam_unix.so file on an infected machine with its own malicious version that accepts a specific backdoor password for all users.
CrackMapExec can enumerate the shared folders and associated permissions for a targeted network.
POWRUNER may collect user account information by running `net user /domain` or a series of other commands on a victim.
Cobalt Strike can [REDACTED] any files or payloads placed on a target machine to help them blend in.
MirrorFace has used tools including the Secure Copy Protocol (SCP) client from PuTTY and Cobalt Strike.
SoreFang can gain access by exploiting a Sangfor SSL VPN vulnerability that allows for the placement and delivery of malicious update binaries.
GlassWorm has masqueraded as legitimate VSCode extensions. GlassWorm has also impersonated Github projects.
Leviathan has sent spearphishing emails with links, often using a fraudulent lookalike domain and stolen branding.
HALFBAKED can obtain information about running processes on the victim.
CURIUM created [REDACTED] instances to facilitate use of malicious domains and other items.
Linfo creates a backdoor through which remote attackers can list contents of drives and search for files.
CSPY Downloader can download additional tools to a compromised host.
Zebrocy collects the OS version and computer name. Zebrocy also runs the `systeminfo` command to gather system information.
During Operation Dream Job, Lazarus Group performed [REDACTED] attacks against administrator accounts.
ccf32 can delete files and folders from compromised machines.
Emotet can download follow-on payloads and items via malicious `url` parameters in obfuscated PowerShell code.
Grandoreiro can parse Outlook .pst files to extract e-mail addresses.
XLoader has exploited Office vulnerabilities during local execution such as CVE-2017-11882 and CVE-2018-0798.
Qilin has named its payload file TeamViewer_Host_Setup to disguise itself as a legitimate TeamViewer file.
Cannon uses SMTP/S and POP3/S for C2 communications by sending and receiving emails.
During Operation Wocao, threat actors archived collected files with WinRAR, prior to exfiltration.
Samurai has been used to deploy other malware including Ninja.
Scattered Spider has registered [REDACTED] to spoof legitimate corporate login portals.
DarkComet can collect the computer name, RAM used, and operating system version from the victim’s machine.
RogueRobin uses [REDACTED].exe to run a .sct file for execution.
Dragonfly has registered [REDACTED] for targeting intended victims.

DarkGate uses a hard-coded string as a seed, along with the victim machine hardware identifier and input text, to generate a unique string used as an internal mutex value to evade static detection based on mutexes.
InvisibleFerret has the capability to query installed programs and running processes. InvisibleFerret has also identified running processes using the Python project “psutil”.
CosmicDuke searches attached and mounted drives for file extensions and keywords that match a predefined list.
LightNeuron contains a function to encrypt and store emails that it collects.
Ke3chang has used network scanning and enumeration tools, including Ping.
GALLIUM used Web shells to persist in victim environments and assist in execution and exfiltration.
PyDCrypt has modified firewall rules to allow incoming SMB, NetBIOS, and RPC connections using `netsh.exe` on remote machines.
Kimsuky has obtained specific Registry keys and values on a compromised host.
Empire can add a SID-History to a user if on a domain controller.
SLIGHTPULSE can deobfuscate base64 encoded and RC4 encrypted C2 messages.
Fox Kitten has accessed victim security and IT environments and Microsoft Teams to mine valuable information.
BRICKSTORM has utilized XOR cipher encryption to hide key strings within their code, to include IPv4 addresses of public DNS-over-HTTPS (DOH) servers.
CosmicDuke collects user credentials, including passwords, for various programs including Web browsers.

TA2541 has registered [REDACTED] often containing the keywords “kimjoy,” “h0pe,” and “grace,” using domain registrars including Netdorm and No-IP DDNS, and hosting providers including xTom GmbH and Danilenko, Artyom.
OilBooster can exfiltrate files to an actor-controlled OneDrive account via the Microsoft Graph API.
CSPY Downloader has attempted to appear as a legitimate Windows service with a fake description claiming it is used to support packed applications.
OilBooster can hide its console window upon execution through the `ShowWindow` API.
During the 3CX Supply Chain Attack, AppleJeus installs a [REDACTED] to execute the POOLRAT macOS backdoor software.
VersaMem encrypted captured credentials with AES then Base64 encoded them before writing to local storage.

Medusa Group has leveraged public facing vulnerabilities in their campaigns against victim organizations to gain initial access. Medusa Group has also utilized CVE-2024-1709 in ScreenConnect, and CVE-2023-48788 in Fortinet EMS for initial access to victim environments.

CANONSTAGER uses the [REDACTED] (TLS) array data structure to store function addresses resolved by its custom API hashing algorithm. The function addresses are later called throughout the binary from offsets into the TLS array.
RogueRobin collects the victim’s username and whether that user is an admin.
ServHelper may attempt to establish persistence via the `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\` run key.
The server component of SystemBC has used various TCP ports for C2 communication.
Maze has issued a shutdown command on a victim machine that, upon reboot, will run the ransomware within a VM.
WhisperGate can make an HTTPS connection to download additional files.
StarProxy has used native windows API calls such as `GetLocalTime()` to retrieve system data.
MiniDuke uses Google Search to identify C2 servers if its primary C2 method via Twitter is not working.
Bad Rabbit has used Mimikatz to harvest credentials from the victim's machine.

BADHATCH can use SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 proxies to connect to actor-controlled C2 servers. BADHATCH can also emulate a reverse [REDACTED] on a compromised machine to connect with actor-controlled C2 servers.
Bisonal's DLL file and non-malicious decoy file are encrypted with RC4 and some function name strings are obfuscated.
During the 2015 Ukraine Electric Power Attack, Sandworm Team installed a modified Dropbear SSH client as the backdoor to target systems.
Linfo creates a backdoor through which remote attackers can delete files.
APT3 has been known to add created accounts to local admin groups to maintain elevated access.
The Winnti for Windows HTTP/S C2 mode can make use of a local [REDACTED].
PureCrypter has used multiple file names to appear legitimate such as firefox\firefox.exe, Google\chrome.exe, and Taskmgr.exe.
Patchwork has used watering holes to deliver files with exploits to initial victims.
Magic Hound has captured the [REDACTED] of visitors to their phishing sites.
Winter Vivern leverages malicious attachments delivered via email for initial access activity.
Empire contains modules that can discover and exploit unquoted path vulnerabilities.
HiddenFace can download files from the C2 to victim systems.
PolyglotDuke can use `LoadLibraryW` and `CreateProcess` to load and execute code.
OSX_OCEANLOTUS.D can use the `touch -t` command to change timestamps.
SysUpdate can contact the DNS server operated by Google as part of its C2 establishment process.

Earlier Pikabot variants use a custom encryption procedure leveraging multiple mechanisms including AES with multiple rounds of Base64 encoding for its command and control communication. Later Pikabot variants eliminate the use of AES and instead use RC4 encryption for transmitted information.
REvil can use [REDACTED] for execution and to retrieve active services.
Saint Bot has been distributed through malicious links contained within spearphishing emails.
SILENTTRINITY can collect start time information from a compromised host.
During C0015, the threat actors use the command `net group "domain admins" /dom` to enumerate [REDACTED].
Waterbear has deleted certain values from the Registry to load a malicious DLL.
LoJax is a UEFI BIOS [REDACTED] deployed to persist remote access software on some targeted systems.
CSPY Downloader can use GET requests to download additional payloads from C2.
Impacket tools – such as `getST.py` or `ticketer.py` – can be used to [REDACTED] using [REDACTED] given a password, hash, aesKey, or TGT.
Chimera has used [REDACTED] scripts to execute malicious payloads and the DSInternals [REDACTED] module to make use of Active Directory features.
GlassWorm has spread through Visual Studio extensions. GlassWorm has also spread through JavaScript projects hosted on Github.

PoetRAT checked the size of the hard drive to determine if it was being run in a sandbox environment. In the event of sandbox detection, it would delete itself by overwriting the malware scripts with the contents of "License.txt" and exiting.
For C0010, UNC3890 actors staged malware on their infrastructure for direct download onto a compromised system.
BADFLICK has captured victim computer name, memory space, and CPU details.
During Cutting Edge, threat actors used multiple web shells to maintain presence on compromised Connect Secure appliances such as WIREFIRE, GLASSTOKEN, BUSHWALK, LIGHTWIRE, and FRAMESTING.
APT1 used the `ipconfig /all` command to gather network configuration information.

Kimsuky has collected victim organization information including but not limited to organization hierarchy, functions, press releases, and others. Kimsuky has also used large language models (LLMs) to gather information about potential targets of interest.
Kazuar finds a specified directory, lists the files and metadata about those files.
APT5 has accessed Microsoft M365 cloud environments using stolen credentials.
InvisiMole can collect data from the system, and can monitor changes in specified directories.
Dragonfly has dropped and executed SecretsDump to dump password hashes.
APT37 has used malware that will issue the command `shutdown /r /t 1` to reboot a system after wiping its MBR.
